top_choice_rationale: P001 honours Katori's magic-wavelength lattice scheme and Ye's realisation of it at 10^-18, a result verified between independent laboratories (JILA, RIKEN, PTB, NIST, SYRTE), with a clean two-name allocation and a citation that can stay clear of the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. It is a judgement of degree that it is new enough, but the physics is mature, reproduced and well understood. P004 follows because it contains the same clock part, though I cannot judge the single-name IceCube part and doubt one name can stand for the observatory. P002 comes next: a striking prediction followed by experiment, but the field is young, the pairing mechanism is open and the omission of Cao, Fatemi and Dean is hard to explain. P003 is real, reproduced physics but a narrower tool-like discovery; no award ranks last.
recusal_note: Long-time close collaborator of Anne L'Huillier (2023 laureate) and co-author with the Lund attosecond group and Keller's group at ETH; none of the credited names in P001-P004 is a collaborator, but my atomic many-body and precision-atomic-physics work is adjacent to the clock proposal, so a possible recusal could be considered.
